evals.prompt: Our `src/billing/discounts.py` module reports 92% line coverage in pytest, yet a `>` vs `>=` off-by-one bug shipped to production. Set up branch coverage and `mutmut` mutation testing to expose and kill the surviving boundary mutants.
evals.expected_output: Configures `pytest --cov=src --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=80` in `pyproject.toml` (`[tool.coverage.run] branch = true`), runs `mutmut run --paths-to-mutate=src/billing/discounts.py`, inspects survivors with `mutmut results` and `mutmut show <id>`, and adds exact threshold boundary tests (`amount == 100`, `amount == 99.99`, `amount == 100.01`) plus return-value assertions to reach >= 75% mutation score.
expectations: Enables `--cov-branch` (`branch = true` in `[tool.coverage.run]`) rather than relying on line coverage alone
Runs `mutmut run --paths-to-mutate=...`, `mutmut results`, and `mutmut show <id>` to inspect surviving mutants
Explains why weak tests (e.g., testing only `amount = 50` and `amount = 200` or asserting `is not None`) let `>` -> `>=` boundary mutants survive
Writes exact boundary-value parametrized tests that kill the off-by-one mutants and targets >= 75% mutation score

evals.prompt: Before refactoring a messy `src/inventory/allocator.py` module that currently sits at 31% branch coverage, build a test-quality safety net and configure `[tool.coverage.run]` / `[tool.coverage.report]` exclusions properly.
evals.expected_output: Configures `[tool.coverage.run]` (`source = ['src']`, `branch = true`, `omit = ['*/tests/*']`) and `[tool.coverage.report]` (`fail_under = 80`, `show_missing = true`, `exclude_lines` for `pragma: no cover`, `if TYPE_CHECKING:`, `raise NotImplementedError`), maps uncovered branches via `--cov-report=term-missing`, writes characterization/edge-case tests BEFORE touching production logic, and validates assertion quality with `mutmut`.
expectations: Insists on raising branch coverage (>= 80%) and killing trivial mutants BEFORE altering `allocator.py` production code
Configures `[tool.coverage.run]` (`branch = true`) and `[tool.coverage.report]` (`fail_under = 80`, `show_missing = true`, sensible `exclude_lines`) in `pyproject.toml`
Targets uncovered error branches, empty collections, and boundary inputs identified by `--cov-report=term-missing`
Audits tests for assertion-free 'smoke' calls that inflate coverage without verifying outputs

evals.prompt: During a `mutmut` run on `src/orders/validator.py`, 4 surviving mutants are logging-message tweaks (`logger.debug(...)`) while 6 are negated guard conditions and altered return constants. How should we triage equivalent/logging mutants vs real test gaps and run this efficiently in CI?
evals.expected_output: Prioritizes killing the 6 logic/guard/constant mutants with stronger behavioral assertions, handles genuine non-behavioral logging mutants via `# pragma: no mutate` (sparingly) or `mutmut` config hooks rather than brittle log-string tests, and runs scoped `mutmut` on changed modules in CI alongside `pytest --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=80`.
expectations: Prioritizes killing logic, guard-condition, and return-value mutants by tightening test assertions
Distinguishes cosmetic `logger.debug` string mutants (handled via `# pragma: no mutate` or `mutmut` filtering) from real behavioral test gaps instead of writing brittle log-text tests everywhere
Scopes `mutmut` runs (`--paths-to-mutate`) for practical CI runtime while running `--cov-branch --cov-fail-under=80` on every PR
Computes mutation score (`killed / total actionable mutants`) against the >= 75% quality bar
